messages:
Sam (sales): Hey team — customer doing a POC asked for our incident response / breach notification timeline and what we can include in the RFP. They want: notification SLA, who we contact, sample IR plan, and what forensic artefacts we can share. Need a short blurb they can include by EOD. Any legal/security constraints?

Maria (security): Hi @Sam — quick summary: we do not provide contractual "breach notification SLA" in self-serve plans, but for enterprise / Dedicated contracts we include notification commitments in the security addendum. For the POC you can provide our standard operational timeline and point-of-contact. :white_check_mark:

Jordan (legal): Add: regulatory timelines (GDPR 72h, certain US state breach laws vary) are statutory and may affect disclosure timing. We cant promise to notify earlier than required without approvals, but we will prioritize high-severity incidents.

Alex (engineering): For technical detail we typically include:
- scope (systems impacted)
- root cause summary
- detection/containment timeline
- remediation actions taken
- indicators (IOCs) if safe to share

Sample timeline we can paste into an RFP (high-level):
```
Detection & initial triage: within hours of detection
Initial customer notification: target 24-72 hours depending on severity & regulatory requirements
Containment & mitigation plan: 1-10 business days depending on complexity
Post-incident report & remediation summary: delivered within 30 days
```

Maria (security): POC notes: we can provide the above as standard. We can also offer a named security contact for the POC (security@redwoodinference.com) and stand up a dedicated Slack/email war-room if requested. We will NOT share raw logs containing customer data without explicit consent + NDA.

Alex (engineering): If the customer requests forensic artefacts, acceptable items (subject to review) include:
- redacted audit logs (timestamps, event types)
- affected instance identifiers (no internal hostnames)
- scope & timeline CSV
- sanitized packet captures if legally approved and consented to by the customer

Jordan (legal): Recommended RFP paragraph (short):
"Redwood Inference maintains an established incident response program. In the event of a security incident affecting customer data, Redwood will prioritize rapid investigation and will provide initial notification to impacted customers in accordance with applicable laws and our contractual commitments. Customers on enterprise agreements can request a named incident response contact and explicit notification timelines via the security addendum."

Sam (sales): Great. Can we include the sample timeline block and the paragraph in the RFP? Also: customer asked whether we notify their parent company security & CSM automatically — what's the flow?

Maria (security): Yes to both. Typical flow for enterprise/POC: detection -> internal IR lead -> notify customer-designated security contact + assigned CSM/AM -> if high severity, exec on-call gets looped in. Add that sentence: "Notifications will be sent to the customer's designated security contacts and the assigned CSM/AM." Keep it concise.

Alex (engineering): Also: for a point-in-time forensic snapshot we require a signed DPA/NDA amendment and will either spin an isolated snapshot in a Dedicated environment or coordinate an export from the customer's private VPC. Call that out in the RFP as "forensic artifacts available subject to legal review and a signed agreement."

ir-bot: Incident template available: `/incident create --template POC-notify`

Sam (sales): Thanks all — I'll draft the RFP entry and paste here for quick signoff before sending. Appreciate the fast turnaround! :pray:
